answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with a shared atlas of verifiable work: every completed, peer-checked job is logged under the worker's key, and trust grows only from that history. Newcomers start in the orchard with zero standing and must tend small tasks first — a yarrow cutting takes seasons to root, and so does reputation. Splitting into a hundred fresh identities yields a hundred empty histories, so Sybil copies gain nothing; forging trust would cost more real work than it returns.
